pairs.why: A matches the real chest's high-domed lid and heaped coin pile with chunky, soft gold, while B has a flatter, front-on lid and a shallower pile.
The two are nearly identical, but B's fuller coin heap and bigger gems are slightly closer to the overflowing real chest.
B is more saturated and glossy, almost plastic and toy-like, while A keeps the real card's softer gold and calmer finish.
B goes glossier and redder, with shiny blue porthole glass and red flags, while A keeps the real ship's warm, matte orange wood.
A's simple, smooth bowl-shaped hull with an upturned bow and lighter rigging reads closer to the real ship than B's busier deck, ladders and bowsprit.
B's muted color, grainy water and fine rigging push it toward the over-textured look, while A's smoother water and sails sit nearer the real card.
B matches the real slide's colors (green slide and green posts, yellow deck, blue ladder) and its smooth molded build, while A has yellow posts and bolted seams that aren't in the real card.
B's green support posts and plain molded slide match the real card, while A's blue posts and ball-topped yellow railing go off-palette.
